findings: The industrial defect-detection/rejection premise is supported, but the selected manipulation sequence is not. The Rovema manual documents photo-eye detection followed by an air-cylinder/push-rod reject, while the Loma source describes stop-on-detect, air blast, pusher, diverter, and related mechanisms. No cited primary source establishes continuous-belt manual/robotic sidewall pinching, level lifting, or tray placement as the real operation. The candidate must characterize those documented alternatives and label sidewall pinch as a proposed representative robotic handling method rather than a sourced industrial sequence, or provide primary evidence for that sequence.

The pinned-YAM construction plan is not numerically actionable. It supplies no carton body/flap/wall dimensions, contents count/size/mass, hinge limits, belt dimensions/speed, tray dimensions/placement, or initial layout. It also defers the essential grasp width to later empirical selection without recording even a testable starting geometry or confirming the pinned YAM gripper envelope. Add explicit SI-unit modeling assumptions and a concrete first-build geometry; proprietary calibration and completed physics results are not required.

The selected candidate is marked "ready" with no missing evidence despite the unresolved essential grasp/access geometry. Its own plan says to choose body width empirically, and its risk admits that flap interference and spill behavior remain unvalidated. For this factual construction gate, readiness should be conditional and the missing dimensional/access checks should be listed rather than represented as fully resolved.

The quoted core evidence is otherwise supported by the acquired primary material: the Rovema manual states that an open-flap detection causes rejection and identifies an air-cylinder/push-rod mechanism; the FEFCO page-8 diagram/text supports one-piece slotted boxes with top and bottom flaps; and the Loma article supports the warning that air-blast rejection is unsuitable for open packages that could spill. No material quotation fabrication was found.
